It's becoming more and more important for scientists to understand English. It is certainly the preferred language for publication since around three-quarters of all scientific research is published in English. This trend is unlikely to change soon, but is the dominance of English in the sciences a bad thing?

But could the dominance of English be the downfall of science? Scientists whose native language is English seem to have an advantage here. It doesn't seem fair that a scientist could work for years on an important piece of research that could change peoples' lives, but they aren't able to share this work with the world because they can't speak English.

What do real scientists think about this issue? This is a hot topic – but in which language should we discuss it?!

  • What is the writer's opinion?

    The writer doesn't give their own opinion on the topic.    The writer thinks that English should be the language of science.    The writer thinks that scientists shouldn't speak English.
